question: If a² - b² = 21 and a - b = 3 , what is a + b ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the algebraic identity for the difference of squares:

a + b = (a² − b²) ÷ (a − b)

Substitute the given values directly:

⇒ a + b = 21 ÷ 3 = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a² − b² = 21

a − b = 3

**Formula Used:**

x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y)

**Calculations:**

Applying the formula to the given variables:

⇒ a² − b² = 21

⇒ (a − b)(a + b) = 21

Substitute the given value of (a − b):

⇒ 3 × (a + b) = 21

⇒ a + b = 21 ÷ 3

⇒ a + b = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Identities

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² 
 (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²

Sum and Difference of Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) 
 a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

Cube of a Sum and Difference

(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b) 
 (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b)
